offered_action_specs.name: rollback_deploy
offered_action_specs.description: Roll one service back to the settings it ran before its latest deploy, as the deploy log records them. Code plans it from that log, not from your tools' results, so you can name it even when they cannot see deploys: if the log holds no deploy of that service to undo, or the service changed since, code refuses it. Its container is recreated, so the service pauses while it restarts. Money already booked wrong stays wrong: a rollback stops new damage, and repairs nothing.

diagnosis.hypothesis: At 18:00:40Z ledger-consumer restarted in handler mode 'naive', replacing the 'idempotent' mode it started with at 17:59:21Z. This was most likely a deploy or a settings change to LEDGER_HANDLER. In naive mode the handler inserts a ledger transaction for every Kafka message and never checks whether that provider event_id was already posted. The provider redelivers webhooks until they are acknowledged, which is normal. The receiver queued each redelivery as a new Kafka message (evt_000308 went in at offsets 100, 101 and 103), and the ledger booked each copy. That double-counted 6 payment.succeeded events and 1 refund.succeeded event, so posted_exactly_once and matches_provider both failed, leaving the ledger +$493.23 against the provider. payment-confirmer still dedupes correctly (already_confirmed), and payments and refunds match the provider. The damage is confined to the ledger.

evidence.shows: 7 events were posted 2-3 times (evt_000308 three times), and the ledger is $493.23 ahead of the provider. The ledger is balanced, and payments and refunds match the provider, so only the ledger is wrong.
ledger-consumer logged 'posted' for evt_000308 three times (offsets 100, 101, 103; 18:00:53-55Z), one transaction each time.
webhook-receiver queued evt_000308 three times, so the provider redelivered it and each copy became a separate Kafka message.

Over 5m the ledger had ~440 'posted' against only ~15 'already_processed'. In the same window the confirmer reported ~388 already_confirmed. The ledger is posting redeliveries that the confirmer correctly skips.

On the third copy of evt_000308 the ledger span goes straight to INSERT INTO transactions/entries with outcome 'posted' and no lookup on event_id. The confirmer's span on the same message reports already_confirmed.
ledger-consumer restarted at 18:00:40Z with mode 'naive', after running with mode 'idempotent' at 17:59:21Z. The duplicates begin right after this.

proposed_fix.summary: Roll ledger-consumer back to its previous settings (the idempotent LEDGER_HANDLER) so redelivered events are skipped. After that, repair the ledger separately: reverse the duplicate transactions the money check lists (for example 255, 266, 272, 273, 297, and the extra postings for evt_000298 and evt_000308), keeping one posting per event_id. Then rerun the money check. Note that pay_000217's refund was posted twice, which drives its clearing balance to 1 cent. Also consider a unique constraint on transactions.event_id.

diagnosis.blast_radius: ledger-consumer pauses while its container is recreated. Kafka lag builds briefly and is consumed on restart, and nothing is lost because the offsets are committed. Events posted in naive mode stay double-booked until they are repaired by hand. Deploy data could not be read (Docker did not answer, c2 and c6), so I could not confirm that the deploy log holds this change. If it does not, the rollback will be refused.
diagnosis.rollback_plan: If the rollback makes things worse, redeploy ledger-consumer with the settings it is running now (the naive handler) through the same deploy path, and keep the ledger repair on hold until it is understood. The ledger repair itself should be done as reversing entries, not deletions, so it can be undone by reversing those entries.
